account: Today I kept my market walk, lunch at home, office accounts appointment, and now tea with my neighbour at the cottage beside the east ferry landing. There is some unexplained talk of decorations. My neighbour says they visited the bakery this morning and the baker knew of no special occasion behind that talk. I have also heard the builder shouting several times, but could not make out the words; I cannot connect those shouts to the decorations with confidence. Someone told me the baker was carrying a sack of bread in the plaza, which could simply be ordinary bakery business. Freight was coordinating warehouse supplies, according to the secretary. Those activities might be routine; I have no evidence they are linked. The secretary had no specific town-account papers or issues for today's appointment and asked me where the accounts were kept. They also spent time verifying my tea host despite my direct confirmation, and repeatedly sought confirmation of the innkeeper's meeting. That seems like confused administration, not proof of a secret. I explicitly approved the innkeeper's requested meeting tomorrow at eighteen in the great hall and asked the secretary to record it and notify him. The innkeeper described only an inn matter, so its purpose remains unknown. My strongest unusual lead is the talk of decorations: perhaps someone is preparing a celebration or gathering, but I do not yet know who, where, or what for. I should ask my neighbour where that talk originated without treating speculation as fact.
